subject: geography
title: Population Policies
welcome_lead: Evaluate China's, Singapore's and Niger's policies.
meta_desc: A-Level Geography adventure on pro-natalist, anti-natalist policies and ethical implications.
final_note: Policies shift but rarely reverse demographic trends.

concepts.def: Policy reducing births; China One Child (1979-2015).
Policy encouraging births; France, Hungary, Singapore.
China 1979-2015; reduced 400 million births but caused gender imbalance.
China 2016; replaced One Child; insufficient to halt decline.
China 2021; even fewer births recorded since.
Selective abortion of female fetuses; China 117:100 male:female at peak.

walkthroughs.body_html: One Child Policy (1979-2015) prevented an estimated 400 million births. Sex-selective abortion left 117:100 male:female ratio by 2000s; 30 million 'missing women'. Two Child (2016) and Three Child (2021) policies failed to raise fertility above 1.3. Population peaked 2021 at 1.41 billion.

Stop at Two (1972) lowered fertility from 4.7 to 1.4. Have Three or More (1987) launched matchmaking, tax incentives, baby bonuses (S$8000-10000). Despite measures TFR fell to 1.04 in 2022 (world's lowest). Highlights how once below replacement, hard to return.

Niger TFR 6.7; government promotes family planning but contraception use just 11 percent. Cultural resistance, religious values, husband consent requirements limit uptake. World Bank funds Sahel Women's Empowerment Project targeting girls' education to reduce fertility.
